_comment: The Scout wake phrases, and the training settings used to build them.
`file` must match the filename in ConduitService.qml's wakePhrasePresets —
nothing enforces that automatically, so if you rename one, rename it there
too. The trained .onnx files go in ~/.local/share/vynx-conduit/wakeword/.
`threshold` is a starting point, not a finding. Measure it: point
scripts/wakeword/wakeword.py --wav at a recording of yourself saying the
phrase, and at half an hour of podcast, and pick the number that separates

phrases.name: hey_scout
phrases.note: The default. The 'hey' prefix gives the model a distinctive onset to anchor on, which is what stops it firing on the word 'scout' in conversation.

phrases.name: okay_scout
phrases.note: Three syllables, the most robust of the three. Longer phrase, lower false-accept rate.

phrases.name: scout
phrases.note: One syllable and a common English word, so the classifier has much less to discriminate on. Held to a stricter threshold than the prefixed phrases for that reason; expect it to still be the one that misfires.

training._note: n_samples is the quality dial. openWakeWord's own quick notebook uses 1000 and says accuracy may be low; the thorough one uses tens of thousands and takes hours. 5000 is a deliberate middle. Raise it and steps together if a phrase misfires after threshold tuning.
